policies.title: South Korean ordinary passports: South Sudan electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: Current Republic of Korea Foreign Ministry South Sudan guidance says ordinary passport holders are not visa-free, visa-on-arrival issuance has stopped, and online visa issuance is available. The South Sudan Interior eVisa service delivers the visa PDF before travel.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Republic of Korea passport holder visiting South Sudan; it does not establish treatment for South Sudanese nationals, dual nationals, diplomatic, official, service, emergency or other travel documents.
The Republic of Korea source reports that visa-free entry for ordinary passports is unavailable and visa-on-arrival issuance has stopped; it identifies online visa issuance as the available route.

Apply through South Sudan's official eVisa service, create an account, submit the visa application and pay online. After approval, download the eVisa PDF before travel; admission and other entry conditions remain for South Sudan authorities.

application.label: South Sudan eVisa application
application.processingTime: The official portal says the eVisa PDF is downloadable within 72 hours.
steps: Create an account on the official South Sudan eVisa service.
Complete the visa application and pay the application fee online.
After approval, download the eVisa PDF before travelling.

unresolved.reason: Current Singapore and South Sudan official sources authenticate the eVisa service, but none directly maps an ordinary Singapore passport to a visitor route. The South Sudan portal asks whether an applicant is eligible; do not infer eligibility from its availability.

Current Japanese Foreign Ministry guidance is a travel prohibition and does not state a Japanese ordinary-passport visa route. South Sudan's eVisa portal is not a nationality schedule, so the eVisa snapshot is not independently established.

Italy's current Foreign Ministry guidance says an entry visa is compulsory but does not say whether Italy's ordinary visitor visa is issued electronically, on arrival or by a mission. Do not collapse a visa requirement into eVisa.

Current Swiss official travel and representation pages do not provide a Swiss ordinary-passport South Sudan visitor-visa route. South Sudan's portal is not an express Swiss eligibility result and cannot supply that missing mapping.

Current Finnish Foreign Ministry guidance directs travellers to destination authorities and does not state a Finnish ordinary-passport South Sudan issuance route. The general eVisa workflow has no Finnish nationality result.

Current Luxembourg government guidance does not state the South Sudan visitor-visa route for an ordinary Luxembourg passport. South Sudan's country table and eVisa service do not fill that nationality-specific issuance gap.

No current Portuguese passport-authority source found a nationality-wide South Sudan visitor-visa issuance result. The South Sudan eVisa portal's general workflow is not proof of Portuguese ordinary-passport eligibility.

No current Austrian passport-authority source found a nationality-wide South Sudan visitor-visa issuance result. A general instruction to consult the destination authority cannot establish the eVisa fallback.

No current Maltese passport-authority source found a nationality-wide South Sudan visitor-visa issuance result. The general South Sudan portal is explicitly eligibility-gated and cannot establish the eVisa fallback.

New Zealand's current South Sudan advice reports security and operational risks but no visitor-visa route. South Sudan's eVisa portal supplies only general pre-travel workflow, not an ordinary New Zealand passport eligibility result.

No current Greek passport-authority source found a nationality-wide South Sudan visitor-visa issuance result. South Sudan's named exemption table does not establish a complementary eVisa rule for ordinary Greek passports.
